5.text: I obtained several sketches of “spirits” of this kind. Fig. 201, a, is the

6.text: “lake-spirit” (hɪthaˊ-kal) of one small lake lying near the seacoast in Anadyr

7.text: Bay. He has the shape of a seal and the hands of a man. His head is

8.text: shaggy, and he comes out of the lake bolt upright. Fig. 201, b, is the “spirit”

9.text: of Holy Cross Bay. He has one hand with only three fingers. Fig. 201, c,

10.text: is the “spirit” of the estuary of the Anadyr. His hair stands erect, and, like

11.text: the last, he has only one hand with three fingers. I was told that the “spirit”

12.text: of the middle course of the Anadyr has one eye and three-fingered hands.

13.text: In Fig. 201, d, the “spirit” of the middle course of the Anadyr is thus

14.text: represented. He has a vertical mouth, one eye, and three-fingered hands.

15.text: Fig. 201, e, a “spirit” living in the sea (aˊnqa-kal), has the body of a fish,

16.text: with a very large shaggy head. On another sketch is represented a large

17.text: sea-spirit, who has very long hair on both his head and his buttocks.

18.text: The “master” of the fish of mountain-brooks is said to have a long thin

19.text: body and a face covered with hair. The “master” of the forest has a body

20.text: of wood, without arms or legs. His eyes are on the crown of his head. He

21.text: moves from place to place, rolling along like a log of wood.

22.text: Pičvuˊčin is a special “owner” of wild reindeer and of all land-game. He

23.text: lives in deep ravines, and stays near the forest-border. From there he sends

24.text: reindeer-herds to the hunters; but when he is angered he withholds the supply.

25.text: He is especially strict in demanding the performance of all ancient customs

26.text: and sacrifices connected with the hunt, and resents every slight neglect of

27.text: them. He is represented as very small, not larger than a man’s finger, and

28.text: his footprints on the snow are like those of a mouse. The Maritime Chukchee
